source.citation: Rappoldt C, Boogaard HL, Brodsky L, Kodesova R, van Diepen CA (2012), Extension of the WOFOST soil water submodel; Comparison with SWAP and technical documentation, EcoCurves report 6
source.source_type: technical report with WatFDGW source appendix

source_bound_method_elements_relevant_to.element: layer water amount as a compact conserved state
source_bound_method_elements_relevant_to.evidence: WATFDGW names WC, water amount per layer, as its main status variable; water content and hydraulic quantities are derived after each update

source_bound_method_elements_relevant_to.element: matric flux potential for dry unsaturated flow
source_bound_method_elements_relevant_to.evidence: for equal soil type the dry interface-flow estimate is the MFP difference divided by centre distance; the report explicitly treats this as a stationary-flow approximation when matric suction dominates gravity

source_bound_method_elements_relevant_to.element: equal-flux interface condition for heterogeneous soils
source_bound_method_elements_relevant_to.evidence: the report states that MFP is discontinuous across material interfaces and solves for an interface suction/pF such that the two half-face fluxes are equal
historical WATFDGW uses robust local bisection with MaxFlowIter rather than a global profile Newton iteration
the MFP-based dry estimate may be positive downward or negative upward
wet unit-gradient limit uses thickness-weighted harmonic conductivity across adjacent layers

source_bound_method_elements_relevant_to.element: root uptake supplied as an external layer sink
source_bound_method_elements_relevant_to.evidence: TRA is calculated by crop routine and passed to the water routine as a given sink

historical_implementation_details_not_to.reason: SWAP5 time is generic and solver substeps must not be calendar-defined

historical_implementation_details_not_to.detail: field capacity as a hard transport regime boundary
historical_implementation_details_not_to.reason: this is a WOFOST reduced water-balance rule, not a general hydraulic identity

historical_implementation_details_not_to.detail: downward flux chosen as max(dry_MFP_estimate, wet_unit_gradient_estimate)
historical_implementation_details_not_to.reason: this asymmetric heuristic is not required by the MFP/equal-flux concept and must be qualified against full Richards if reused

historical_implementation_details_not_to.detail: upward dry flow capped at 0.50 of the equal-potential water transfer per daily step
historical_implementation_details_not_to.reason: the report introduces the 0.50 fraction to suppress day-step gradient reversal; it is timestep-specific stabilization rather than physical law

historical_implementation_details_not_to.detail: upward flow rejected or clipped according to field-capacity/groundwater cases
historical_implementation_details_not_to.reason: SWAP5 requires symmetric bidirectional exchange without hidden clipping

historical_implementation_details_not_to.detail: SUBSOL as separate groundwater-to-bottom-layer capillary-rise routine
historical_implementation_details_not_to.reason: SWAP5 direct groundwater coupling requires an explicit bottom head/flux interface and generic coupling windows

historical_implementation_details_not_to.detail: top-down filling to field capacity during initialization and wet redistribution
historical_implementation_details_not_to.reason: historical WOFOST bookkeeping choice, not a required LayeredMFP state representation

historical_implementation_details_not_to.detail: fixed interpolation tables and legacy Fortran record/array structures
historical_implementation_details_not_to.reason: SWAP5 may use shared immutable constitutive providers, SoA layouts and worker-local scratch

important_source_limitations: the report explicitly says MFP itself is discontinuous across soil-type interfaces; only suction/head is continuous
the dry MFP-gradient estimate neglects gravity and is justified mainly for dry conditions
the report acknowledges that its groundwater capillary-rise limitation may be too restrictive in realistic shallow-groundwater situations

the historical heterogeneous-interface bisection and separate equal-potential transfer bisection are local iterations; predictable runtime therefore depends on an explicit iteration cap rather than the label non-iterative
WOFOST was designed as an efficient crop water-availability model rather than a precise profile-physics replacement for SWAP

layeredmfp_design_consequences.primary_face_contract: derive one conservative realized face flux from both endpoint states and both material hydraulic providers
layeredmfp_design_consequences.heterogeneous_interface: solve a bounded local equal-flux interface state or use a prequalified equivalent representation; never subtract MFP values across unlike materials directly
layeredmfp_design_consequences.persistent_state_candidate: layer water storage plus only genuinely required auxiliary physical state; no permanent root-finder scratch
layeredmfp_design_consequences.forcing_and_sinks: surface fluxes and distributed sinks remain external inputs to the soil-water step
layeredmfp_design_consequences.time: all transport/update rules scale with generic dt; no daily 0.5 equalisation rule
layeredmfp_design_consequences.groundwater: historical SUBSOL semantics are donor evidence only, not the SWAP5 bottom-interface contract
layeredmfp_design_consequences.reference: full Richards remains qualification reference for every retained reduced-order approximation
